title: Learn visual representations without class labels
subtitle: Hide part of the scene and ask for it back: train a masked-image decoder, watch a teacher collapse and recover, predict a feature instead of pixels, then probe what the frozen encoder knows.

What did the encoder learn? A linear probe

legendTitle: The same colours; the rows are now patches of the scene
provenance: Scope: the encoder is Vision I's, frozen (Vision I trained it with labels to answer whether a mug is on the right), with named axes{{axes}}. Vision II trains only small parts on top of it: a 32-number MAE decoder, a 22-number I-JEPA predictor, a 15-number DINO head and a 3-number probe line, all in a seeded numpy script (train_vision2.py) whose results the page recomputes. One 8×8 scene, four hidden patches, three to four training images. Real MAE, DINO and I-JEPA train the whole encoder on millions of images; the box in section 1 lists what this toy can and cannot show.
